newsitem.title: USA: Brazil global bond priced attractively-US analysts. [CORRECTED 16:52 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Brazil global bond priced attractively-US analysts. [CORRECTED 16:52 GMT]

text.p: Brazil's 30-year global bond pleased investors with its somewhat higher-than-expected spread (corrects from price) and established a new long-term benchmark for the country, U.S. analysts said Wednesday.

"It's a good pricing. The Brazilian government did a good job by getting a lot of the bonds out at a good rate for market participants," said Raul Elizalde, head of quantitative analysis at ING Barings.

Brazil priced the $3.0 billion issue at 395 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries and offered it in exchange for "C" bonds, Discount bonds and Par bonds, as well for direct cash purchase, said lead managers Goldman Sachs and J.P. Morgan.
"The major benefit was probably to define a long-dated benchmark for Brazil," said Kurt Schmid, head of proprietary trading at SBC Warburg.
In the secondary market, the global quickly tightened about 20 basis points, bid up by dealers who had swapped their Bradies at lower-than-market value, analysts said.

Brazil exchanged the issue for $1.622 billion of Discounts, $542 million of Pars, $86 million of "C" bonds and $750 million of cash. That should free between $550 million and $620 million of collateral, based on various estimates.
"The Brazilian government was a little more generous, but the trade-off was they got a lot more out and were able to retire a lot of Bradies," Elizalde said.

Analysts said the makeup of the Brady exchange was about as expected, since Brazil had set a more-attractive swap price on Discounts and Pars than on "C" bonds. Some experts were surprised any "C"s had been exchanged.
"Given the price and the structure of the transaction, it was not surprising that primarily Discount and Par bonds have been converted," SBC Warburg's Schmid said.
Cash purchases offered the most attractive investment alternative because of the almost certain instant profit, analysts agreed.
The lead managers said they received bids for about $16 billion of direct purchases, but final allocations limited cash acquisitions to 25 percent of the issue.

"Clearly the best alternative was to submit non-competitive cash offers, given basically this free profit derived from the fact that the pricing in the exchange for the Bradies was below market and had to be compensated," Schmid said.
Looking ahead, analysts said they expected the global bond would tighten further.
After opening at 93.234, the price could climb toward the 97 level in the near term, some analysts said. At 1030 EDT/1430 GMT, the issue was trading at about 95 bid, they said.
"We're pretty optimistic near- to medium-term, partly on the basis of technicals," said Richard Segal, head of fixed income research at at Santander Investments.
Investors in new bonds and swaps tend to bid somewhat cautiously, leaving room for appreciation, Segal said.
